sources: No effect: the simulator moves the same life forward (learned flows and public trends, docs/simulator.md).

description.EN: Study a two-year master's before you start working.
description.ES: Estudiar un máster de dos años antes de empezar a trabajar.

sources: Tuition: scenario-assumptions.csv (scenario S001), annual_tuition_chf p25 / p50 / p75 as a distribution (the luck of the decision picks the percentile; good luck = cheaper); 2 years (study_duration_years). Keys tuition.monthly.*.

Salaries: employed income p25 / p50 / p75 (synthetic-profiles.csv) scaled to the age of entry with the BFS LSE 2024 age curve (22 if you start now, 24 after the master's). Keys salary.startNow.*, salary.afterMaster.*.
No master's wage premium: the dataset has no education level and the BFS table we use is by age and position, so both paths pay the same at the same age. The only difference is the age of entry.
Living while studying: the flow model (students spend about 21 % less; the event's tuition replaces the learned one).

title.EN: Go for a management job in Zurich
title.ES: Buscar un puesto de dirección en Zúrich

description.EN: Apply for a management role at your company's Zurich office. You would have to move; the pay depends on the level you get, and the flat on how lucky you are.
description.ES: Optar a un puesto de dirección en la oficina de Zúrich de tu empresa. Tendrías que mudarte; el sueldo depende del nivel que consigas, y el piso, de la suerte que tengas.

sources: Catalogue S013 + S021. Pay rise: BFS LSE 2024, median wage of each management level / all positions at age 40 (ratio.promotion.*).
New rent: rent model learned from synthetic-profiles.csv (household x city), at the p75 / p50 / p25 of the dataset spread.
Living costs in Zurich: flow model city factors (groceries, restaurants, utilities...). Pay does not depend on the city in the dataset.
Career: SENIOR follows the BFS management curve from then on.

sources: Pay: employed income p25 (the offer now) and p25 / p50 / p75 after searching (income.EMPLOYED.*, synthetic-profiles.csv, rounded to 100).

sources: Income while unemployed: median unemployed income / median employed income in synthetic-profiles.csv (ratio.unemployed). The dataset gives the unemployed almost no income; real Swiss unemployment insurance pays more, but it is not in our data.

Chance per two-year turn: the Swiss unemployment rate of the age group (Eurostat une_rt_m, 5-year mean) used as the chance of losing your job during the turn (assumption); the month it happens is drawn within the turn.
